extracted.intended_audience: Recipients of Federal financial assistance (elementary/secondary schools, postsecondary institutions), their Title IX coordinators, administrators, and legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory standards for implementing the Department of Education's final Title IX regulations, with specific provisions on effective date, transition assistance, and a newly codified prohibition on retaliation (§106.71).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date timing and APA minimum
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Administrative Procedure Act (APA), the effective date for final regulations cannot be fewer than 30 days after publication in the Federal Register unless a statutory exception applies; the Department determined no exception justified an earlier effective date and set the effective date of these final regulations as August 14, 2020.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department believes 60 days would be sufficient ordinarily but considered exigent circumstances (COVID-19) and other comments; it declined multiple staggered effective dates because that would cause confusion and some provisions in §106.44 reference §106.45. Recipients were on notice for more than two years and will receive technical assistance during the transition and after the effective date to assist with compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory text controls over prior guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent these final regulations differ from any Department guidance documents (including the 2001 Guidance, 2017 Q&A, the withdrawn 2011 Dear Colleague Letter and 2014 Q&A), the final regulations, when effective, are controlling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NPRM and preamble explain departures from prior guidance; commenters asking whether prior guidance is rescinded are answered by: final regulations control when effective, and prior guidance documents have been expressly withdrawn where noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attorney use by recipients (optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each recipient may choose to use attorneys to advise the recipient on compliance with these final regulations but is not required to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department's RIA addresses the costs of attorneys for recipients; the Department believes litigation may decrease as a result of these final regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retaliation prohibited (§106.71) — core prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: No recipient or other person shall intimidate, threaten, coerce, or discriminate against any individual for the purpose of interfering with any right or privilege secured by Title IX or its implementing regulations, or because the individual has made a report or complaint, testified, assisted, or participated or refused to participate in any manner in an investigation, proceeding, or hearing under Title IX and its implementing regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision is purposefully broad and applies to complainants, respondents, witnesses, and others who participate or refuse to participate. The Department added §106.71 to expressly prohibit retaliation and modeled language similar to §100.7(e) (Title VI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of retaliation — non-sex code violations arising from same facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Charges or sanctions against an individual for code of conduct violations that do not involve sex discrimination or sexual harassment, but arise out of the same facts or circumstances as a report or formal complaint of sex discrimination or sexual harassment, constitute retaliation if imposed 'for the purpose' of interfering with any right or privilege secured by Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: punishing a complainant for underage drinking arising out of the same incident may be retaliation if done to interfere with reporting. If a recipient neutrally applies a zero-tolerance policy equally in all cases, imposing the same punishment would not be 'for the purpose' of interfering and thus not retaliation. Recipients may adopt amnesty policies to encourage reporting; §106.71 does not create amnesty but does not preclude it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of identities
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must keep the identity of any individual who has made a report or complaint of sex discrimination (including complainants, respondents, and witnesses) confidential except as may be permitted by FERPA (20 U.S.C. 1232g and 34 CFR part 99), as required by law, or to the extent necessary to carry out the purposes of the regulations implementing Title IX (including investigations, hearings, or judicial proceedings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unnecessary exposure of identities may lead to retaliation; confidentiality is required subject to the listed exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing retaliation complaints under grievance procedures (§106.8(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaints alleging retaliation may be filed according to the 'prompt and equitable' grievance procedures for sex discrimination that recipients are required to adopt and publish under §106.8(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department agrees recipients may process retaliation allegations under their established Title IX grievance procedures; the preamble clarifies the relationship between §106.71 and §106.8(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient responsibility and available measures to address retaliation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department will hold a recipient responsible for responding to allegations of retaliation; the recipient's response depends in part on its relationship with the person committing retaliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the retaliator is a student or non-employee third party, the recipient may take measures such as pursuing discipline against a student or issuing a no-trespass order against a third party. Recipients should process allegations in accordance with equitable grievance procedures and take appropriate measures to the extent possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: No actual knowledge requirement for retaliation claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The actual knowledge requirement that applies to sexual harassment in §106.44 does not apply to a claim of retaliation; the Supreme Court has not applied an actual knowledge requirement to retaliation claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.71 contains no requirement of actual knowledge; however §106.44(a) clearly requires that a recipient with actual knowledge of sexual harassment must respond promptly in a manner that is not deliberately indifferent.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Amendment carve-out
rubrics_metrics.description: The exercise of rights protected under the First Amendment does not constitute retaliation as defined in these final regulations; the Department may not require recipients to restrict First Amendment rights to prohibit retaliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This protects lawful speech; the Department recognizes First Amendment does not restrict private schools but the Department itself is subject to the First Amendment and will not administer regulations in a way that violates it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materially false statement exception and safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: Charging an individual with a code of conduct violation for making a materially false statement in bad faith in the course of a grievance proceeding under the regulations implementing Title IX does not constitute retaliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, a determination regarding responsibility alone is not sufficient to conclude any party made a materially false statement in bad faith. §106.45(b)(2)(B) requires written notice of allegations to inform parties of any provision in the recipient's code of conduct that prohibits knowingly making false statements or knowingly submitting false information during the grievance process. Recipients retain discretion in handling false statements but must avoid treating determinations of responsibility as proof of bad faith.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retaliation coverage of third parties and non-employees
rubrics_metrics.description: The retaliation prohibition may apply even when the person engaging in retaliatory acts is not an employee of the recipient (e.g., a respondent's friend who is not a student or affiliated with the recipient).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should respond to such complaints to the best of their ability even if they cannot require the person accused of retaliation to participate in the recipient's equitable grievance procedures; appropriate measures may include no-trespass orders or other actions within the recipient's authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarifying changes to remedies reference (§106.3(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department revised §106.3(a) to remove reference to monetary damages as a possible remedy ordered by the Assistant Secretary when investigating a recipient for violations of Title IX or its implementing regulations, referring instead to the Department's authority to enforce Title IX pursuant to 20 U.S.C. 1682.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change addresses commenters' concerns about remedies described in the NPRM; the preamble explains the rationale for removing monetary damages as a listed remedy in §106.3(a).
